pr.title: coverage: Carve out hole spans in a separate early pass
pr.description:
When extracting spans from MIR for use in coverage instrumentation, we sometimes need to identify *hole spans* (currently just closures), and carve up the other spans so that they don't overlap with holes.

This PR simplifies the main coverage-span-refiner by extracting the hole-carving process into a separate early pass. That pass produces a series of independent buckets, and we run the span-refiner on each bucket separately.

There is almost no difference in the resulting mappings, other than in some edge cases involving macros.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: Coverage span extraction was refactored so closure "hole" spans are removed by an early bucket-carving pass instead of being handled inside the main SpansRefiner. Holes are collected separately, merged when overlapping/adjacent, and used to split initial coverage spans into ordered buckets; each bucket is re-sorted and refined independently. This is a behavior-changing refactor, not a confirmed bug fix; mapping output changes only in macro edge cases.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `mir_to_initial_sorted_coverage_spans` returned a single flat `Vec<SpanFromMir>`. Closure-like statements were emitted as spans carrying `is_hole: true`, sorted together with ordinary spans using span position/dominance, then handed to `SpansRefiner`. The refiner itself carved holes out: if `prev.is_hole` it dropped `curr`; if `curr.is_hole` it called `carve_out_span_for_hole`, pushing a pre-hole span and mutating `prev` to start after the hole; finally it discarded hole spans with `self.refined_spans.retain(|covspan| !covspan.is_hole)`. The PR describes this as: "This PR simplifies the main coverage-span-refiner by extracting the hole-carving process into a separate early pass. That pass produces a series of independent buckets, and we run the span-refiner on each bucket separately."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The pre-PR transformation being replaced is the historical handling of hole spans inside the main sorted span-refinement walk: keep closure hole spans in the same flat, globally sorted list as ordinary spans (tagged `is_hole`), and carve them during refinement by dropping overlapping `curr` spans, emitting pre-hole pieces, and mutating `prev` to skip past a hole. This older logic is the differential variant, not a newly invented wrong rewrite. In macro edge cases it produced different mappings than the new early bucket-carving pass: the supplied `closure_macro.cov-map` expectation changes from `Number of file 0 mappings: 6` to `5`, replacing a mapping ending `to (start + 0, 18)` with one ending `to (start + 0, 15)`. The PR explicitly says: "There is almost no difference in the resulting mappings, other than in some edge cases involving macros."
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions instrumented for coverage (`-C instrument-coverage`) whose MIR contains closure-like statements, especially closures inside macro expansions. Relevant inputs are source spans extracted from MIR basic coverage blocks, including closure assignment spans treated as holes, ordinary statement/terminator spans, signature spans, and macro-expanded spans. Triggering cases are functions where a closure/hole span overlaps or is adjacent to other coverage spans, and macro cases such as `tests/coverage/closure_macro.cov-map` and `tests/coverage/closure_macro_async.cov-map`.
analysis.trigger: A function body contains at least one closure-like statement, so coverage span extraction must carve a hole out of other coverage spans; overlapping or adjacent holes and macro-generated spans make the ordering/fragmentation behavior observable.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled and coverage spans are being extracted from MIR for instrumentation.
The function body contains at least one closure-like statement identified as a hole span (`is_closure_like(statement)`).
Spans may overlap or be adjacent to holes, and may cross a hole so they need to be split into before/after fragments.
Bucket contents must remain sorted for the subsequent SpansRefiner, and holes must not appear in final code mappings.
pitfalls: Do not leave hole spans in the flat list handed to the main refiner after moving hole carving to an early pass; the refiner now assumes it never sees holes.

Merge overlapping or adjacent holes before carving (`holes.dedup_by(|b, a| a.merge_if_overlapping_or_adjacent(b))`); otherwise the same region can be carved repeatedly and fragments can be lost or misordered.

When a span crosses a hole, split it into both parts: `split_around_hole_span` returns the strictly-before part via `trim_end` and the strictly-after part via `trim_start`; keep the after-fragment for the next hole.
Carry leftover fragments into the next hole and finally append remaining initial spans as the last bucket, so spans after the final hole are not dropped.
Re-sort every bucket after carving; the source notes the refiner expects each bucket to be 'internally sorted'.
`trim_start`/`trim_end` must preserve the syntax context of `self`, not `other`, and return `None` when there is no valid trim; unit tests cover spans before/at/inside/after the other span.
The fake signature span condition must account for holes as well as spans: the PR changes it to `if !initial_spans.is_empty() || !holes.is_empty()`.

Macro-span cleanup (`remove_unwanted_macro_spans`, `split_visible_macro_spans`) no longer needs to special-case holes because holes are extracted separately; reintroducing hole guards there indicates the separation is incomplete.
analysis.testStrategy: Use coverage-mapping regression tests that assert exact `.cov-map` contents, especially `tests/coverage/closure_macro.cov-map` and `tests/coverage/closure_macro_async.cov-map`; compare mapping counts and each mapping's span endpoints (the PR changes 6 mappings to 5 and a `start + 0, 18` endpoint to `start + 0, 15`). Add unit tests for the span-trimming primitives with relative positions well-before/before/start/mid/end/after/well-after, and use a different `SyntaxContext` on `other` to verify the result keeps `self`'s context. For differential testing, use two otherwise identical Rust sources differing only in whether a closure/hole is placed so that a coverage span crosses it, ideally inside a macro, then compare the generated coverage mappings.
